worlds.title: Origins
tagline: Where living things begin
What separates the living from the merely complicated

modules.title: What is Life?
hook: A rock and a beetle are both made of atoms. Only one of them runs away.
Every definition of life you have been given has an exception. Find one that doesn't.

specimens.title: Sorting Tray
specimens.unlocks: Sort any specimen into alive, not alive, or argue
blurb: A tray for sorting things into alive and not alive.
Sorts specimens against the seven signs — and flags the ones that refuse to sort.

specimens.title: The Seven Signs
specimens.unlocks: Test any specimen against all seven signs at once
blurb: The seven things living things do.
The standard checklist, with every exception it fails on written on the back.

specimens.title: Flame Jar
specimens.unlocks: Compare any process against burning
blurb: A fire that grows, eats and breathes — and is not alive.
The classic counter-example: metabolism-like behaviour with no organisation and no heredity.

specimens.title: Spark Flask
specimens.unlocks: Run the 1953 experiment and see exactly what it gives you
blurb: The flask that made the beads life is built from.
Miller–Urey, reproduced honestly: monomers out, nothing alive, and the gap left visible.

modules.title: Cells
hook: What if a whole city had to fit inside something smaller than a grain of sand?
Fit a working city — power, walls, instructions, transport — into 20 micrometres.

specimens.title: Scale Lens
specimens.unlocks: Zoom any diagram down to cell size
blurb: A lens that shows how big things really are.
Renders any structure at true relative scale.

specimens.title: Membrane
specimens.unlocks: A wall you can put round anything
blurb: A wall that chooses what gets in.
A selectively permeable bilayer. Needed to build anything that stays alive.

specimens.title: Mitochondrion
specimens.unlocks: Powers builds in later modules
blurb: The bit that makes the power.
Turns glucose into ATP. Every build with a running cost needs one.

specimens.title: Nucleus
specimens.unlocks: Stores instructions for World 2
blurb: Where the instructions are kept.
Holds the genome. Required before you can read or edit a gene.

specimens.title: Ribosome
specimens.unlocks: Build proteins in World 2
blurb: The machine that follows instructions.
Translates mRNA into protein. This is what lets you build a protein later.

modules.title: Biomolecules
hook: Four kinds of building block make every living thing you have ever seen.
Sugars, fats, proteins, nucleic acids. Four families, all of life.
lessonTitles: Why Oil and Water Won't Mix

specimens.title: Family Key
specimens.unlocks: Identify any molecule as one of the four families
blurb: A key that tells you which family a molecule belongs to.
Sorts any biological molecule into carbohydrate, lipid, protein or nucleic acid.

specimens.title: Glucose Ring
specimens.unlocks: Fuel any build that has a running cost
blurb: The ring that holds the energy.
Stored chemical energy in bond form. Feeds every process with an upkeep.

specimens.title: Lipid Drop
specimens.unlocks: Build any boundary or store
blurb: The drop that will not mix in.
The hydrophobic effect made portable: builds membranes, stores and insulation.

specimens.title: Peptide Chain
specimens.unlocks: Start any protein build
blurb: A string of beads that folds itself up.
An unfolded polypeptide. Sequence in; shape, and therefore function, out.

worlds.subject: life

worlds.title: The Code
tagline: The instructions inside you
Information storage, retrieval, and manufacture

modules.title: DNA
hook: Two metres of instructions, folded into something you cannot see.
Two metres of polymer per cell, packed 10,000-fold, read without tangling.

specimens.title: Packing Spool
specimens.unlocks: Fold any long thing into a small space
blurb: The spool that fits two metres into a dot.
Hierarchical coiling: DNA onto histones, onto fibres, onto chromosomes.

specimens.title: Base Set
specimens.unlocks: Write any sequence
blurb: The four letters everything is written in.
A, C, G and T. Enough alphabet for every organism that has ever lived.

specimens.title: Replication Fork
specimens.unlocks: Copy any sequence you hold
blurb: The place where the ladder splits in two.
Semiconservative replication: each old strand templates a new one.

specimens.title: Error Lens
specimens.unlocks: Spot copying errors in any sequence
blurb: A lens that finds the letters that went wrong.
Highlights substitutions, insertions and deletions against a reference.

specimens.title: Unwinder
specimens.unlocks: Read a gene without breaking the strand
blurb: The tool that unwinds without knotting.
Topoisomerase in specimen form: relieves supercoiling ahead of the fork.

modules.title: Genes
hook: Why do you have your grandmother's eyes and nobody else's laugh?
The same genome builds a neuron and a liver cell. What decides?

specimens.title: Gene Tag
specimens.unlocks: Label any stretch of sequence with its job
blurb: A tag that says what a piece of DNA is for.
Marks reading frames, promoters and regulatory regions on a sequence.

specimens.title: Switch Board
specimens.unlocks: Turn genes on and off in any cell
blurb: The switches that decide which pages get read.
Regulatory control: why a liver cell and a neuron share a genome and share nothing else.

specimens.title: Allele Pair
specimens.unlocks: Cross any two organisms and predict the result
blurb: Two copies of the same instruction, one from each parent.
Diploidy, dominance and recessiveness, made testable with a cross.

specimens.title: Pedigree Chart
specimens.unlocks: Trace any trait through a family
blurb: A chart for following a trait through a family.
Standard pedigree notation. Distinguishes dominant, recessive and sex-linked patterns.

modules.title: Proteins
hook: A string of beads folds itself into a machine. Nobody tells it how.
Sequence determines structure determines function. Break any link and see.

specimens.title: Folding Rig
specimens.unlocks: Fold any sequence and watch it find its shape
blurb: The rig that lets a string fold up on its own.
Nothing directs the fold: the sequence and the water do all of it.

specimens.title: Shape Gauge
specimens.unlocks: Test whether a folded protein can do its job
blurb: A gauge that checks if the shape is right.
Function follows conformation. Change the shape and the job goes.

specimens.title: Active Site
specimens.unlocks: Catalyse any reaction you have the enzyme for
blurb: The notch that only one thing fits into.
Substrate specificity and transition-state stabilisation, in one component.

specimens.title: Chaperone
specimens.unlocks: Rescue a protein that folded badly
blurb: The helper that stops proteins folding wrong.
Chaperone protein. Prevents aggregation — the failure behind several diseases.

specimens.title: Assembled Enzyme
specimens.unlocks: Proves you can go from sequence to working machine
blurb: A working machine you built from beads.
Sequence to fold to function, assembled end to end without a shortcut.

worlds.subject: life

worlds.title: Change
tagline: How living things become different
Variation, selection, and time

modules.title: Evolution
hook: Nobody designed the eye. So how did it get so good?
Descent with modification: the only mechanism that makes design without a designer.
lessonTitles: The Same Bones in Different Jobs

specimens.title: Two Lenses
specimens.unlocks: Examine any claim as observation or as inference
blurb: Two lenses: one for what you saw, one for what you worked out.
Separates directly observed claims from inferences about the unobserved, and asks what each would take to overturn.

specimens.title: Limb Set
specimens.unlocks: Compare the parts of any two limbs
blurb: Four limbs that do different jobs with the same bones.
Bat, whale, mole and human forelimbs, alignable part for part.

specimens.title: Core Sample
specimens.unlocks: Read any layered rock as a sequence
blurb: A tube of rock with the layers still in order.
A stratigraphic core. Carries the sequence, and leaves its cause open.

specimens.title: Sequence Reader
specimens.unlocks: Compare any two genomes and build a tree
blurb: A reader that lines up two sets of instructions.
Aligns sequences and scores similarity, including shared damage.

specimens.title: Change Gauge
specimens.unlocks: Measure how far a population has moved
blurb: A gauge for how far something has changed.
Distinguishes change within a population from the contested extrapolation beyond it.

modules.title: Natural Selection
hook: Change the weather. Watch which beetles are left.
Three conditions produce selection automatically. Remove one and it stops.

specimens.title: Pale Beetle
specimens.unlocks: Run selection on any trait you hold
blurb: A beetle that got eaten for being the wrong colour.
The specimen that failed the three conditions. Carries the mechanism with it.

specimens.title: Fitness Dial
specimens.unlocks: Score any trait against a named environment
blurb: A dial that shows what counts as good here.
Fitness is relative to an environment, not a property of an organism.

specimens.title: Moth Pair
specimens.unlocks: Compare two forms of one species side by side
blurb: Two moths, one pale and one dark.
Biston betularia, both morphs. Counted year by year for over a century.

specimens.title: Resistant Strain
specimens.unlocks: Stress-test any medicine you design
blurb: The germ the medicine could not kill.
A resistant isolate. Turns every later drug build into a selection problem.

modules.title: Development
hook: One cell becomes a whole animal. Where are the instructions for 'leg'?
How a single cell partitions itself into an addressed, patterned body.
lessonTitles: The Same Toolkit in a Fly and in You

specimens.title: First Division
specimens.unlocks: Start any body from a single cell
blurb: The moment one cell becomes two.
The first cleavage. Everything downstream is division plus difference.

specimens.title: Gradient Strip
specimens.unlocks: Tell any cell where it is
blurb: A strip that tells a cell where it is.
A morphogen gradient: position encoded as concentration.

specimens.title: Hox Set
specimens.unlocks: Lay out the axis of any body plan
blurb: The same set of instructions a fly uses.
Hox genes, colinear and deeply conserved. Same toolkit, different animal.

specimens.title: Body Blueprint
specimens.unlocks: Proves you can lay out an animal from scratch
blurb: A plan for a whole animal.
Axes, segments and appendage placement, assembled and stress-tested.

worlds.subject: life

worlds.title: Bodies
tagline: The machine you live inside
Systems, failure modes, and repair

modules.title: Human Body
hook: Everything in you is moving right now. Even the bits that feel still.
Eleven systems, one budget, no downtime for maintenance.

specimens.title: Cell Census
specimens.unlocks: Count the cells in any body
blurb: A counter for how many cells you are.
Cell census by tissue, including the bacteria that are not yours.

specimens.title: Heart Model
specimens.unlocks: Circulate anything round a closed loop
blurb: A pump that runs your whole life without stopping.
Four chambers, two circuits. The pressure gradient does the rest.

specimens.title: Gas Swap
specimens.unlocks: Exchange gases across any surface
blurb: The place where the air swaps over.
Alveolar exchange. The urgent half of breathing is getting carbon dioxide out.

specimens.title: Gut Tube
specimens.unlocks: Break any food down into parts you can use
blurb: A tube nine metres long, folded up inside you.
The alimentary canal: controlled disassembly, then selective absorption.

specimens.title: Signal Web
specimens.unlocks: Connect any two systems you have built
blurb: The messages the parts send each other.
Endocrine and neural signalling. No organ works alone, and none can be tested alone.

modules.title: Nutrition
hook: Your lunch becomes you. Follow it and find out how.
Trace a molecule of glucose from plate to muscle to heat.

specimens.title: Fuel and Bricks
specimens.unlocks: Split any food into energy and materials
blurb: Food is both fuel to burn and bricks to build with.
Separates the caloric and the structural roles of an intake.

specimens.title: Digest Trace
specimens.unlocks: Follow any meal through the whole tube
blurb: A trace that follows food all the way through.
Tracks a bolus from mastication to absorption, enzyme by enzyme.

specimens.title: Citrus Crate
specimens.unlocks: Cure a deficiency in any body you build
blurb: The crate of lemons that stopped sailors dying.
Lind's 1747 trial in specimen form — arguably the first controlled clinical experiment.

specimens.title: Study Sieve
specimens.unlocks: Filter any health claim by evidence quality
blurb: A sieve for telling good advice from bad.
Grades a claim by study design, confounding and effect size.

modules.title: Immunity
hook: Something got in. You have about six hours.
An army with no central command that must not attack its own country.

specimens.title: Barrier Set
specimens.unlocks: Defend any body you have built
blurb: The walls that stop most things getting in.
Innate barriers: skin, mucus, acid, temperature. Most of defence, none of it clever.

specimens.title: Antibody
specimens.unlocks: Tag any invader for destruction
blurb: A tag that sticks to one invader and nothing else.
Adaptive specificity: one clone, one target, and a memory afterwards.

specimens.title: Vaccine Vial
specimens.unlocks: Train immunity without the disease
blurb: A way to learn the lesson without getting ill.
Antigen without virulence. Produces memory at a fraction of the risk.

specimens.title: Self Marker
specimens.unlocks: Distinguish your own cells from invaders
blurb: The label that says 'this one is yours'.
MHC self-presentation. Autoimmunity is this discrimination failing.

specimens.title: Immune Stack
specimens.unlocks: Proves your defence survives a real challenge
blurb: A whole defence you put together yourself.
Layered innate and adaptive response, stress-tested against live challenges.

modules.title: Neuroscience
hook: Your thoughts are electricity moving through wet meat. That is not an insult.
Eighty-six billion cells, no clock, no supervisor, and yet: you.
lessonTitles: Your Brain Edits What You See

specimens.title: Action Potential
specimens.unlocks: Send a signal down any nerve
blurb: A spark that runs down a nerve.
An all-or-nothing depolarisation wave. Information is in the rate, not the size.

specimens.title: Synapse
specimens.unlocks: Connect any two neurons
blurb: The tiny gap the message has to jump.
Chemical transmission across a cleft — which is what makes the connection adjustable.

specimens.title: Illusion Card
specimens.unlocks: Test any perception against the input
blurb: A picture that proves your eyes lie to you.
Demonstrates that perception is inference, not transmission.

specimens.title: Recall Trace
specimens.unlocks: Compare a memory with what happened
blurb: A memory changes a little every time you use it.
Reconsolidation: retrieval rewrites. Why eyewitnesses drift and why testing beats re-reading.

specimens.title: Reflex Arc
specimens.unlocks: Proves you can build a working circuit
blurb: A circuit that acts before you have thought.
Sensory neuron, interneuron, motor neuron. No brain required, and that is the point.

modules.title: Disease
hook: Most of the time your body wins. What happens when it doesn't?
Every disease is a mechanism failing in a specific, findable way.

specimens.title: Cause Sorter
specimens.unlocks: Classify any illness by what causes it
blurb: A sorter for what actually made you ill.
Infectious, genetic, deficiency, degenerative, environmental — and the overlaps.

specimens.title: Spread Model
specimens.unlocks: Model transmission through any population
blurb: A model of how something passes from person to person.
Contact rate, transmissibility and duration. R0 falls out; it is not put in.

specimens.title: Case Map
specimens.unlocks: Find the source of any outbreak
blurb: A map of who got ill and where.
Snow's Broad Street pump generalised: find the source from the pattern of cases.

specimens.title: Eradication Kit
specimens.unlocks: Test whether a disease can be eliminated
blurb: The kit that got rid of one disease for good.
Smallpox eradication. Checks the conditions: no animal reservoir, stable antigen, good vaccine.

modules.title: Medicine
hook: You have a fever. Should you get rid of it?
Every treatment is a trade. Learn to see the other side of the trade.

specimens.title: Candidate Set
specimens.unlocks: Screen molecules against any target
blurb: A tray of molecules, one of which might work.
Screening for binding and for delivery. Most failures are delivery.

specimens.title: Control Arm
specimens.unlocks: Test any treatment honestly
blurb: The other group, who did not get the medicine.
Randomised control. Without it, recovery and treatment cannot be told apart.

specimens.title: Resistance Clock
specimens.unlocks: Predict how long any drug will keep working
blurb: A clock counting down on a medicine.
Selection pressure applied to a pathogen population. Usage rate sets the pace.

specimens.title: Treatment Plan
specimens.unlocks: Proves your treatment survives trial and resistance
blurb: A treatment you designed and tested properly.
Target, delivery, trial design and resistance management, assembled together.

worlds.subject: life

worlds.title: The Living World
tagline: Everything else that is alive
Populations, partnerships, and consequences

modules.title: Plants
hook: A tree is mostly made of air. Find out which part.
Photosynthesis: the reaction that made an oxygen atmosphere and everything after.
lessonTitles: The Plumbing That Has No Pump

specimens.title: Chloroplast
specimens.unlocks: Power any build from light alone
blurb: The green bit that eats light.
Light to chemical bond. The entry point for almost all energy in the biosphere.

specimens.title: Water Column
specimens.unlocks: Move water upward without a pump
blurb: Water climbing a tree with nothing pushing it.
Cohesion-tension: evaporation at the top pulls an unbroken column up.

specimens.title: Leaf Section
specimens.unlocks: Optimise any surface for capture and loss
blurb: A leaf, sliced to show why it is that shape.
The area trade-off: maximise light capture, minimise water loss.

specimens.title: Flower Model
specimens.unlocks: Strike a deal with any pollinator
blurb: A flower is an advert with a payment attached.
Reward, signal and specificity. Coevolved contracts, sometimes cheated.

specimens.title: Whole Plant
specimens.unlocks: Proves your plant survives real conditions
blurb: A plant you built that stays alive.
Roots, transport, leaf and reproduction, tested against drought and shade.

modules.title: Animals
hook: Why does a mouse's heart beat so much faster than yours?
Body size sets metabolism, lifespan, and heartbeat. The scaling law is brutal.
lessonTitles: Big, Small, and Why It Matters

specimens.title: Trade-off Scale
specimens.unlocks: Weigh any two competing demands
blurb: A scale that shows what a body gave up.
No design is free: speed costs armour, size costs agility.

specimens.title: Scaling Rule
specimens.unlocks: Predict what changes when size changes
blurb: Why a mouse and an elephant cannot be the same shape.
Surface area scales as the square, volume as the cube. Almost everything follows.

specimens.title: Gait Set
specimens.unlocks: Move any body you have built
blurb: All the ways of getting about without wheels.
Walking, swimming, flying, burrowing — each with its cost curve.

specimens.title: Instinct Card
specimens.unlocks: Give any animal a behaviour it never learned
blurb: Something an animal knows without being taught.
Fixed action patterns: heritable, selectable, and modifiable by learning.

modules.title: Microbiology
hook: There are more of them on your hand than there are people on Earth.
Most life is microbial. Most of it we have never grown in a lab.
lessonTitles: The Ones That Live in You

specimens.title: Microbe Scale
specimens.unlocks: See anything too small to see
blurb: Most living things are too small to see.
Scale bar from millimetre to nanometre, with the whole domain in between.

specimens.title: Generation Timer
specimens.unlocks: Run selection at bacterial speed
blurb: Some things have babies every twenty minutes.
Generation time as the rate-limiter on evolution. Days become millennia.

specimens.title: Microbiome Swab
specimens.unlocks: Sample the microbes on any body
blurb: The tiny things living on you right now.
Community sampling. More of them than of you, and mostly not optional.

specimens.title: Culture Plate
specimens.unlocks: Grow and count any microbe
blurb: A plate for growing things you cannot see.
Selective media and colony counting — one colony, one founding cell.

modules.title: Ecology
hook: Remove the wolves. Watch the river change shape.
Every population is held in place by forces you can only see by removing them.

specimens.title: Food Link
specimens.unlocks: Connect any two organisms by what eats what
blurb: A line from one thing to the thing that eats it.
The unit of a food web. Direction matters; energy only goes one way.

specimens.title: Trophic Ladder
specimens.unlocks: Work out how many predators any system supports
blurb: Why there are never many lions.
Roughly a tenth carries up each level. That single number sets pyramid shape.

specimens.title: Capacity Line
specimens.unlocks: Find the ceiling of any population
blurb: Every population hits a ceiling.
Carrying capacity as a consequence of limiting resources, not a fixed constant.

specimens.title: Keystone
specimens.unlocks: Test which species any system cannot lose
blurb: The one you cannot take out.
Keystone species: disproportionate effect relative to abundance.

specimens.title: Living Web
specimens.unlocks: Proves your ecosystem survives losing a species
blurb: A whole web you built that keeps working.
Assembled web, stress-tested by removal. Redundancy is what survives.

modules.title: Environmental Science
hook: The air you breathe out today will be in a leaf next spring.
Carbon, nitrogen and water move in closed loops. We opened some of them.

specimens.title: Carbon Tracer
specimens.unlocks: Follow a carbon atom anywhere it goes
blurb: Follow one carbon atom all the way round.
Atmosphere, ocean, biosphere, rock. Fluxes and residence times.

specimens.title: Energy Budget
specimens.unlocks: Balance energy in against energy out
blurb: A small change in temperature is not a small change.
Radiative balance: small forcing, large integrated consequence.

specimens.title: Last Specimen
specimens.unlocks: Records what cannot be recovered
blurb: The last one there ever was.
An irreversible loss. Every other specimen here can be rebuilt; this one cannot.

specimens.title: Intervention Kit
specimens.unlocks: Test any fix for what it breaks
blurb: A fix that does not break something else.
Every intervention has second-order effects. This one makes you find them first.

worlds.subject: life

worlds.title: Frontier
tagline: Biology we are still inventing
Where the field is actively unfinished

modules.title: Biotechnology
hook: We taught bacteria to make human insulin. Here is how.
Borrowing cellular machinery to manufacture things evolution never made.

specimens.title: Host Cell
specimens.unlocks: Run any process inside a living factory
blurb: A cell doing a job you gave it.
An engineered host. Cheaper than chemistry, and it self-replicates.

specimens.title: Thermal Cycler
specimens.unlocks: Amplify any sequence you hold
blurb: A machine that copies DNA over and over.
PCR. Doubling per cycle turns one molecule into billions in an afternoon.

specimens.title: Sequencer
specimens.unlocks: Read any genome you collect
blurb: A machine that reads the whole instruction book.
High-throughput sequencing. Cost per genome fell faster than computing power.

specimens.title: Recombinant Vial
specimens.unlocks: Manufacture any protein at scale
blurb: Medicine made by germs doing what you told them.
A human gene in a bacterial host — the first recombinant drug, and still the model.

modules.title: CRISPR
hook: Bacteria invented gene editing to fight viruses. We took the scissors.
A bacterial immune memory, repurposed into programmable molecular surgery.

specimens.title: Guide RNA
specimens.unlocks: Aim an edit at any sequence
blurb: Scissors that check before they cut.
The guide strand supplies the address; the nuclease supplies the cut.

specimens.title: Phage Record
specimens.unlocks: Records what a bacterium remembered
blurb: Germs invented this to fight viruses.
A CRISPR array: captured viral sequence, kept as adaptive immune memory.

specimens.title: Target Lock
specimens.unlocks: Verify any edit before you make it
blurb: Making sure you cut the right one.
Specificity checking against the whole genome, not just the intended site.

specimens.title: Off-Target Log
specimens.unlocks: Audit any edit for unintended cuts
blurb: A list of the cuts you did not mean to make.
Off-target and mosaicism record. The germline question sits here too.

specimens.title: Edited Genome
specimens.unlocks: Proves your edit worked and did nothing else
blurb: A gene you changed on purpose.
A verified edit: intended change present, off-target audit clean.

modules.title: Synthetic Biology
hook: If you could design a living thing from scratch, what would you make?
Treating the cell as a platform: parts, devices, and the limits of the metaphor.

specimens.title: Part Registry
specimens.unlocks: Draw standard parts for any build
blurb: A box of standard biological parts.
Characterised, composable parts. Standardisation is the whole idea.

specimens.title: Gene Switch
specimens.unlocks: Build logic into any organism
blurb: A switch built out of genes.
A toggle or oscillator. Logic implemented in transcription.

specimens.title: Minimal Cell
specimens.unlocks: Establish the floor for any organism
blurb: The fewest instructions something can live with.
A minimal genome. Notably, a fraction of its genes have no known function.

specimens.title: Designed Organism
specimens.unlocks: Proves your design survives contact with reality
blurb: Something you designed that actually lives.
Specified, built, and tested — including against what it does when it escapes.

modules.title: Space Biology
hook: Your bones start dissolving after two weeks in space. Why?
Every system in you is calibrated to 1g. Remove it and watch what was load-bearing.

specimens.title: Microgravity Rig
specimens.unlocks: Test any body without gravity
blurb: What happens to a body with no up.
Bone loss, fluid shift, muscle wasting. Gravity turns out to be a signal.

specimens.title: Habitability Card
specimens.unlocks: Score any world for life
blurb: A card for scoring whether somewhere could hold life.
Liquid water, energy gradient, chemistry, shielding, stability.

specimens.title: Tardigrade
specimens.unlocks: Survive conditions that kill everything else
blurb: An animal that survives being frozen, boiled and put in space.
Cryptobiosis. Redefines the envelope, without redefining what life needs to run.

specimens.title: Closed System
specimens.unlocks: Proves your life support closes the loop
blurb: A garden that has to keep you alive with nothing coming in.
A closed ecological system. Everything cycles or the crew dies.

modules.title: Future Biology
hook: What should we build, now that we can build almost anything?
The open problems, the live arguments, and the questions with no answer yet.

specimens.title: Scaffold
specimens.unlocks: Grow tissue in any shape you need
blurb: A shape for cells to grow into.
A seeded scaffold. Vascularisation remains the limiting problem.

specimens.title: Recovered Sequence
specimens.unlocks: Reconstruct a genome from fragments
blurb: Instructions rescued from something long gone.
A degraded ancient genome. What comes back is a close approximation, not the original.

specimens.title: Ethics Frame
specimens.unlocks: Ask the question capability cannot answer
blurb: Being able to do something is not a reason to.
Separates the technical question from the question of whether to proceed, and keeps both open.

specimens.title: Your Design
specimens.unlocks: Proves you can justify what you build, not just build it
blurb: The thing you would make, and why.
A final open build. Judged on the reasoning as much as the organism.

worlds.subject: life

worlds.title: Motion
worlds.subject: physics
tagline: How things get from here to there
Position, velocity and acceleration — the three words that describe every move

modules.title: Describing Motion
hook: A ball rolls. How do you tell someone exactly what it did?
A ball rolls across the floor. Without a stopwatch and a tape, can you say what happened?

specimens.title: Ruler
specimens.unlocks: Measure position in any simulation
blurb: A ruler. It tells you where things are.
A calibrated reference for position — every measurement in physics starts here.

specimens.title: Stopwatch
specimens.unlocks: Measure time intervals in any simulation
blurb: Counts the seconds while things move.
Resolves time intervals. Needed whenever you want to know how fast.

modules.title: Graphs of Motion
hook: A line on a page can show a whole journey.
A flat line, a slope, a curve — each one is a journey told in ink.

specimens.title: Graph Paper
specimens.unlocks: Plot any measurement against time
blurb: Paper with a grid. You draw journeys on it.
A calibrated grid for plotting one quantity against another.

worlds.title: Forces
worlds.subject: physics
tagline: Why things start, stop and turn
Pushes and pulls — and the three rules that govern them

modules.title: Newton's Laws
hook: Push a trolley. Push it twice as hard. What changes?
A trolley, a push, and a question: what exactly does the push do?
lessonTitles: The First Rule: Things Keep Going
The Second Rule: Push and Acceleration
The Third Rule: Every Push Has a Pull

specimens.title: Spring Scale
specimens.unlocks: Measure force in any simulation
blurb: A spring that stretches when you pull. The stretch is the force.
A calibrated spring — Hooke's law made tangible. Measures force in newtons.

specimens.title: Force Arrow
specimens.unlocks: Show pushes and pulls on any object
blurb: An arrow that shows a push.
A vector: direction and magnitude. The language of force.

modules.title: Friction and Gravity
hook: Why does a rolling ball ever stop?
Nothing pushes back on a rolling ball — yet it stops. Something must.

specimens.title: Inclined Plane
specimens.unlocks: Split gravity into components in any sim
blurb: A ramp. It turns falling into sliding.
A plane that resolves gravity into parallel and perpendicular components.

worlds.title: Energy
worlds.subject: physics
tagline: The currency of change
What moves moves, what stops stops — and the books always balance

modules.title: Kinetic and Potential
hook: A ball at the top of a hill has not moved yet. What does it have?
A ball sits still at the top of a hill. It has no speed. What does it have?

specimens.title: Energy Meter
specimens.unlocks: Read kinetic and potential in any sim
blurb: A dial that reads how much energy something has.
Resolves kinetic and potential energy in real time.

modules.title: Conservation
hook: Energy never appears. Where did it come from?
A moving thing stops. Its energy did not vanish — so where is it?

specimens.title: Heat Sensor
specimens.unlocks: Find dissipated energy in any sim
blurb: Sees the heat that lost energy becomes.
Detects thermal radiation — the final form of dissipated energy.

worlds.title: Waves
worlds.subject: physics
tagline: How a wiggle travels
Sound, light, ripples — all the same trick, repeated

modules.title: Oscillation
hook: Push a swing. Let go. Why does it come back?
A swing, pushed once, returns. Something pulls it back — what?

specimens.title: Pendulum
specimens.unlocks: Show periodic motion in any sim
blurb: A weight on a string. It swings and swings.
A simple harmonic oscillator — the prototype of every rhythm in physics.

modules.title: Wave Properties
hook: Drop a stone in water. The water does not move outward — but something does.
A stone drops in water. A ripple crosses the pond. No water crosses with it. What moved?
lessonTitles: Loud and Quiet, Bright and Dim

specimens.title: Ripple Tank
specimens.unlocks: Visualise waves in any sim
blurb: A tank of water. You see the waves on it.
A shallow tank for observing wave propagation, reflection and interference.

worlds.title: Fields
worlds.subject: physics
tagline: The invisible that reaches across space
Gravity, electricity, magnetism — three things that act without touching

modules.title: Gravity Fields
hook: The Earth pulls you. Nothing touches you. What is doing the pulling?
You fall. The ground is not pushing you. The air is not pushing you. What is?
lessonTitles: Why the Moon Does Not Fall

specimens.title: Field Line
specimens.unlocks: Draw invisible forces in any sim
blurb: A line that shows where a force points.
A directed line representing field direction. The vocabulary of action at a distance.

modules.title: Electricity
hook: A wire, a battery, a bulb. What is flowing?
A battery, a wire, a bulb. Something moves in the wire. What is it?

specimens.title: Ammeter
specimens.unlocks: Measure current in any circuit
blurb: A dial that reads what is flowing.
Measures current in amperes. Placed in series.

specimens.title: Voltmeter
specimens.unlocks: Measure push in any circuit
blurb: A dial that reads the push.
Measures potential difference in volts. Placed in parallel.

modules.title: Magnetism
hook: A magnet pulls iron. It does not pull copper. Why?
A magnet pulls iron through air. It does not pull copper through air. What is the difference?

specimens.title: Compass
specimens.unlocks: Find field direction in any sim
blurb: A needle that points. Always points.
A magnetised needle on a pivot — aligns with any magnetic field.

worlds.title: Modern Physics
worlds.subject: physics
tagline: Where the simple story breaks down
Very fast, very small, very heavy — and the rules change

modules.title: Relativity
hook: If you run fast enough, does the light go faster?
You chase a beam of light. No matter how fast you run, it pulls away at the same speed. How?
lessonTitles: Time Is Not the Same for Everyone

specimens.title: Light Clock
specimens.unlocks: See time dilation in any sim
blurb: A clock made of light. It ticks differently when it moves.
A photon bouncing between two mirrors — the thought experiment that derives time dilation.

modules.title: Quantum
hook: An electron goes through two holes at once. Which one?
An electron is fired at a wall with two holes. It goes through both. How do we know? The pattern on the other side.
lessonTitles: A Particle That Is a Wave

specimens.title: Double Slit
specimens.unlocks: Show wave-particle duality in any sim
blurb: Two holes in a wall. The simplest experiment that breaks common sense.
The apparatus that forces wave-particle duality into the open.

subjects.title: Life Sciences
tagline: Learn biology by operating the mechanism before naming it.
Twenty-five modules across six worlds, ages 5 to 16.

subjects.title: Physics
tagline: Learn physics by pushing things and watching what happens.
Six worlds from motion to quantum, ages 5 to 16.
